findings.requirement: No trigger-visible counter or transfer outcome may depend on another tenant's rows.
findings.evidence: Create two databases with accounts ('one','a',100), ('one','b',0). Add audit(rowid,tenant,key,source,target,amount)=(40,'two','private','x','y',999) only to the second. Install: CREATE TRIGGER guard AFTER INSERT ON audit WHEN NEW.key='next' BEGIN SELECT CASE WHEN last_insert_rowid()>2 THEN RAISE(ABORT,'counter limit') END; END; Call transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k'), then the same request with key='next'. Both first calls succeed. The second call succeeds without foreign history, leaving balances 80/20, but raises IntegrityError with foreign history, leaving 90/10. CLI independently reproduces exit 0 versus exit 2. Logging instead of rejecting records counters 1,2 versus 1,42; foreign rowid 80 produces 1,82. Pre-repair succeeds in all variants with counters 1,2, matching native tenant-only SQLite. Preserving globally allocated rowids now carries protected insertion history into subsequent trigger execution. This reproducer has no new-row collision or auxiliary rowid reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the repaired sparse-history references while preventing protected allocation history from affecting subsequent trigger counters and outcomes. Add the two-transfer API/CLI regression. If this conflicts with the permitted new-row allocation behavior, obtain an explicit coordinator resolution before acceptance.

Independently verified the admitted R2 repair with 24 API/CLI cases covering transfers and audit, native SQLite controls, sparse references, protected-row preservation, replay, rollback, schema preservation and integrity_check.
Confirmed pre-repair sparse references remain at 100; current and native SQLite correctly update them to 90.
Independently reproduced R3 through API and CLI, with pre-repair and native controls.
Used Python 3.14.3 and SQLite 3.50.4, disposable workspace databases and Python -B; modified no source, tests or instructions.

Assessment focused on the bounded repair and affected original-contract behavior; unrelated exploration was not repeated.
